title: Helper-briefing skill and helper answer standard that carry over to every later session (owner, D-094 R307-R315)
objective: Two new files, no other change. (1) .claude/skills/dispatch-brief/SKILL.md: a short project skill (frontmatter name and description so it is offered for helper dispatch) that turns the orchestrator's question into a helper brief with five named parts: the exact answer or deliverable needed (and the decision it serves); the exact scope (repository, branch, pinned commit, files, records, reference cases); the evidence that could change the answer (what to open first, what would reverse a first conclusion, disconfirming checks); what is unknown and must stay unknown; the depth (lookup, evaluation, decision) and when to stop; plus the fixed return contract (answer first; each finding tied to its evidence and to what it changes; verified facts, reported claims, inferences, assumptions and unknowns kept apart; what was not checked; all parts in ONE hand-back; END-OF-REPORT) and the project's standing clauses (D-093 research clause, reference cases, read-only or builder limits, ports, heavy-run lock, no model override). The skill never shows the owner the brief and never adds work the question did not ask for. (2) .claude/rules/helper-briefing.md: an always-loaded rule (no paths frontmatter, like research-and-verification.md) with two short halves: for the main session, every helper question goes through /dispatch-brief (or its template) before dispatch; for every helper, the answer standard. Kept short (always-loaded size). No change to CLAUDE.md, agents, hooks or settings.
business_reason: The owner asked that helper questions be briefed in the style of the full-picture prompt so answers come back better, and that later sessions do it by themselves without being told again (D-094 R307-R315).

acceptance_scenarios.then: valid frontmatter (name, description); the five brief parts and the return contract are named; nothing asks for owner-facing output
no paths frontmatter (always loaded); the main-session half names /dispatch-brief; the helper half states the answer standard; short

acceptance_scenarios.given: a fresh session in this repository
acceptance_scenarios.then: the rule is in its start-time instructions (always-loaded rules) and the skill is listed; nothing depends on chat history

acceptance_scenarios.given: one real dispatch brief made with the skill after it lands
acceptance_scenarios.then: each part present; the helper's return leads with the answer and keeps facts, claims, inferences, assumptions and unknowns apart
it passes (or reports the size within the owner's rule; the cap was lifted, question B1)

risks: The auto-mode classifier may refuse a .claude write: the owner's words are captured (D-094 R307-R315); retry once under them, never bypass.
A subagent inherits its parent's start-time instructions: this session's helpers see the rule only through their brief; later sessions load it at start.
path_notes: Governance (writes under .claude/); orchestrator-produced like M0-T193; independent G3 by code-reviewer; no file shared with any task in flight.
